subject: Dedicated capacity: BioProspect model memory & quantization impact
messages:
From: Carlos Morello <carlos.morello@bioprospect.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — long-context support and expected QPS

Tessa,

Thanks for the demo earlier. To summarize our requirements: BioProspect wants a dedicated pool for our clinical annotation assistant. Key constraints:
- Model(s): prefer open weights derived from Llama-style family; primary candidate is a 34B variant we tested internally, fallback to a 13B for lower-latency endpoints.
- Peak concurrent requests (inference): ~18 concurrent sessions during batch windows, average steady-state concurrency ~6.
- Request profile: many long-context sessions — we regularly keep ~48k tokens of convo context and expect some sessions to reach 65k tokens in peak usage.
- Throughput: typical QPS ~12 across sessions, bursts to ~40 for batch exports.
- Latency SLO: 2.5s p95 for interactive flows; batch can be slower.

Attached: bioprospect_requirements.pdf (detailed usage patterns) and qps_profile.csv (sample traffic).

We need a sizing recommendation: how many GPUs of what class, recommended quantization profile to control cost, and migration/fallback plan if larger contexts push us over GPU memory. Also share any notes about KV cache offload, model varianting, and fallback to smaller quantized models.

Can you route to the engineering team for an initial memory & fleet estimate? We are on a procurement cycle and would like a committed capacity proposal within 7 business days.

Thanks,
Carlos Morello
Head of ML Platforms, BioProspect
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Morello <carlos.morello@bioprospect.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — long-context support and expected QPS

Carlos — thanks, received. Looping in Karthik and Priyom for sizing. Quick clarifying questions before we size:
1) Are the 65k-token sessions dominated by read-only context (reference docs) or active back-and-forth dialogue that requires frequent KV cache updates?
2) For the fallback 13B, do you expect functional parity or is that purely a stop-gap for high-throughput batch jobs?
3) Any regulatory constraints requiring on-premise deployment (some of our customers choose private deployments which affects GPU selection)?

If you can answer those, Karthik/Priyom will put together a rough fleet plan and recommended quantization profiles. We’ll aim to get a committed capacity sketch and cost delta within 5 business days.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-31T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: BioProspect sizing sketch — memory math and quantization options

Folks — I pulled together a preliminary sizing sketch based on Carlos' profile (34B primary, 13B fallback) and the long-context numbers. Notes and assumptions up front:
- Model footprints (RAM on GPU for weights, approximate):
  - 34B FP16 baseline: ~68GB for weights in VRAM (rough estimate using 2 bytes/parameter + optimizer-free inference footprint).
  - 13B FP16 baseline: ~26GB.
- KV cache sizing (per token stored KV for self-attention): approximate formula used: KV_bytes_per_token = 2 * hidden_size * bytes_per_param_layer_factor. Practically this yields:
  - 34B: KV ~0.0012 GB/token -> 48k tokens ~= 57.6 GB of KV. 65k tokens ~= 78 GB of KV.
  - 13B: KV ~0.00045 GB/token -> 48k tokens ~= 21.6 GB of KV. 65k tokens ~= 29.25 GB of KV.
- Total VRAM need (weights + KV + workspace/activations + driver overhead): add ~15% headroom.

Sizing outcomes (single-inference instance, no offload):
- 34B, FP16, 48k tokens: 68 (weights) + 57.6 (KV) + 12 (workspace) ≈ 137.6 GB -> recommend H100-80GB with NVMe or multiple GPUs / offload. Not feasible in single 80GB slot without KV offload.
- 34B, int8/nf4 quantized (weights): weights reduce ~2.5x -> weights≈27GB, KV still resident unless we offload; with KV at 57.6GB total ≈ 27+57.6+10 ≈ 94.6GB -> still >80GB but could be supported with KV offload to host memory or NVMe (adds latency).
- 34B with aggressive NVMe-backed KV offload and int8 weights: doable on an 80GB A100/H100 with 10–20% latency penalty for p95.
- 13B, FP16, 65k tokens: 26+29.25+6 ≈ 61.25GB -> fits on an 80GB GPU comfortably. Quantized 13B (int8/nf4) drops weights to ~10–12GB giving ample headroom.

Recommendations (tradeoff-driven):
1) Fleet mix approach (recommended for cost/availability):
   - Committed pool: 6x A100/H100-80GB nodes configured for int8 (Q4/NF4) on the 34B variant with KV offload enabled. This supports steady-state concurrency ~6 and handles bursts with autoscaling. Expect average p95 latency at ~2.3–3.0s depending on offload penalty.
   - Buffer capacity: additional 4x 80GB nodes for peak bursts and canary traffic (burst headroom to reach ~18–22 concurrency).
   - Fallback pool: 8x 48GB-class GPUs (e.g., A40-48GB or 48GB A100) running 13B quantized models for sub-1.5s p95 interactive flows or when KV offload would exceed latency SLOs.
2) Quantization profile: use per-channel int8 (Q4) for 34B as default; for high-throughput batch jobs, consider NF4/int4 packed kernels for cost savings. Document a rollout plan and quality/regression tests.
3) KV offload strategy: prefer NVMe-backed offload with async prefetch for longest contexts. For the most latency-sensitive endpoints, route to the 13B fallback (no offload) to meet p95.
4) Autoscaling & routing: implement workload-aware routing — interactive sessions pinned to GPUs with less KV offload; background batch jobs allowed to use offloaded nodes.
5) Contract/commit ask: recommend initial committed footprint = 6 committed-80GB nodes + 8 fallback-48GB nodes for a 12-month term. This maps to the concurrency and provides an upgrade path.

Cost/ops notes: quantization reduces committed GPU weight memory allowing fewer high-memory GPUs but increases engineering/validation work (quality/regression). Offload reduces GPU count but adds NVMe cost and slightly higher p95 latency.

I can produce a node-by-node cost estimate if sales wants to convert to a committed sku. Also recommend setting up a prompt/metric regression suite to validate int8/nf4 rollouts against your QA prompts.

— Karthik
Senior Inference Engineer


From: Carlos Morello <carlos.morello@bioprospect.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — long-context support and expected QPS

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Answers to your clarifying questions:
1) Context is mixed but ~70% is read-heavy documents (medical records, guidelines) that don't change frequently once loaded into the session; ~30% is active dialogue.
2) 13B fallback is acceptable for interactive endpoints where strict p95 is required. We will accept some quality delta there.
3) No on-prem requirement for now — cloud dedicated pool is fine.

We are comfortable with the recommended fleet mix. Please proceed with a committed capacity proposal (6x 80GB + 8x 48GB) and a short SOW describing offload expectations and latency tradeoffs. I'll also share the procurement timeline — procurement needs a signed SOW within 10 business days for Q3 onboarding.

Attaching the detailed requirements again for your records.

Carlos
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Morello <carlos.morello@bioprospect.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — long-context support and expected QPS

Carlos — great, thanks for the confirm. Next steps and owners: 
- Karthik: produce a per-node cost and a short SOW draft covering KV offload, quantization validation, canary rollout plan (ETA: 2 business days).
- Priyom: map procurement SKUs and reserved-commit pricing; include upgrade rules if BioProspect wants to move to H100 later (ETA: 3 business days).
- Stephanie (CS ops): prepare onboarding timeline and required SOC2 evidence checklist for procurement (ETA: 2 business days).

I’ll prepare the committed capacity quote (deal_id DP-2028-014) and loop in our legal and finance once Karthik/Priyom confirm node-level cost. Attaching our standard Dedicated commit template for signatures: Redwood-dedicated-commit-template.docx.

Action items for BioProspect: sign-and-return SOW draft and provide QA prompt set (to run quantization regression). Once we have those, we’ll provision a canary pool and run quality checks before full cutover.

Thanks everyone — closing this thread into an internal task list and sales ticket.

Best,
